goal: Settle the foundations of the git-workflow plugin (the checked GitHub and tool behaviours, the token service and the component declaration) so that the tool image, release core, daily loop, monorepo and retirement phases can be detailed on checked ground.

review_focus.focus: The done check counts report rows; it does not test that a row marked confirmed rests on a run against the sandbox. A claim about the behaviour of an App token must not be confirmed from documentation alone.

The sandbox repository may use settings (repository ruleset against organisation ruleset, plan tier) that differ from the consuming projects, so a confirmed row can fail in production. Each row should name the settings it was run under.
The done check counts rows only. The splitsh-lite linkage and libgit2 rows must be checked against the release binary version the image will pin, not against whichever version is newest.
The note must stay a contract and a decision record. Server code or deployment scripts of the token service would exceed what the concept settled, and no done check catches that.

The declaration must hold a single source for a component's paths (the workspace graph or an explicit list per component), and its single-repository case (one component at the root) must be written out. No done check reads the note for either.

The verify run proves that the pinned versions are in the image, but not that a wrong checksum fails the build. The build must stop on a mismatch, with no fallback download and no latest tag, and nothing from the old Dockerfile (Node, the Gemini and Claude installs, gh-wf, libgit2-dev, openssh-client) may remain.

No done check reads the argument lists of the calls. The installation token must reach the container by environment variable name, never in an argument, a log line or a file, and there must be no fallback to a host binary (concept decision D35).

The verify run cannot show that the machine is clean in every respect, only that git-cliff and splitsh-lite are absent from the host path and that the image runs. The developer states which machine it was run on.

abstract.summary: The plan opens the git-workflow plugin by closing what the milestone m1-foundations asks for: every verify claim of the white paper is checked against GitHub and the real tools, the token service interface, developer authentication, hosting and key custody are settled, and the component declaration is settled. Later phases for the tool image, release core, daily loop, monorepo and retirement are outlined only, one per later milestone of the roadmap.
abstract.outcome: Five notes in the concept's notes directory, one of them recording the sandbox: one with a row per marked line of the white paper for the GitHub App behaviours, one for the tool and ecosystem claims, one for the token service contract with authentication, fallback and hosting, and one for the component declaration with its path resolution and pre-release handling. The milestone gate of m1-foundations can then be read off these notes.
abstract.cost: Nine tasks in the detailed phases: the five tasks of P1, all done, and four in P2 (pins, Dockerfile and compose file, the library function, the clean machine check). The four outlined phases after P2 cost nothing until they are detailed in an amend.
abstract.risks: Several GitHub behaviours the release rests on are unverified and may be refuted, which would change decided concept decisions (the App as the only bypass actor, the GitHub Release created by the App, --latest=false). T1.1 needs a test GitHub App and a sandbox repository that the developer registers first. The token service has no design yet and every remote write depends on it. The white paper marks 18 lines against the concept's 13 claims; the plan covers all 18 and does not reconcile the concept's count.
abstract.success: Each marked line of the white paper has a row with a result and evidence, each refuted claim names the decision it puts in doubt, and the developer can read the token service contract and the component declaration as settled. The milestone m1-foundations gate can then be called met.

tasks.title: Write the commit command: a conventional message drafted by the provider

inputs.why: provider_run_prompt and provider_available, how the host session drafts text

tool_run, which runs the commit in the tool image
remote_identity, the identity of the developer for the commit

verify.from: environment fact: a given message is linted and committed, a bad message is refused, and the drafted message is shown and committed only after the confirmation
verify.run: bash -n bin/modules/git/commit.sh && bash tests/git-commit/run.sh

tasks.why: A developer commits with a conventional message without writing it by hand, and no message reaches the history unseen (decisions D8, D10 and D18 of the concept).
tasks.result: The command app git commit that stages the named paths, drafts or takes a conventional message, lints it and commits.
tasks.done: With --message the command lints that message and commits; without it the command asks provider_run_prompt for a draft from the staged diff, shows it and commits only after the developer confirmed; a message that fails lint-commit is never committed.

A refused lint or a declined confirmation commits nothing and leaves the index as it was. tests/git-commit/run.sh runs it with a stub provider command on a throwaway repository. tasks.title: Write the rules library: the rulesets of the master, release and legacy branches

inputs.why: the classic rules this library replaces; the .github/branch-protection.yaml it read is removed
the permission sets the token service knows: contents, pull-requests and administration, the set the rulesets need

verify.run: bash -n bin/lib/rules.sh && bash tests/git-rules/build.sh

tasks.why: Rulesets replace the classic branch protection and the Stage Guard, so the rules of a repository are one declared set the developer reads and the App applies (decisions D17, D26 and D31).
tasks.result: A library that builds the three rulesets as GitHub ruleset JSON from one declaration and the GIT_WORKFLOW_STAGE switch.
tasks.done: rules_json master development gives a ruleset without required checks, master production requires a pull request, the aggregate check and squash merge, release and legacy give pull request, linear history and the App as the only bypass actor, and an unknown name or stage is refused.
tasks.fails: The development phase would require checks that block direct pushes, or the production rules would not require the aggregate check, or a human could push to the release branch.

brief.arguments: Write bin/lib/rules.sh with rules_load <file>, rules_json <name> <stage> and rules_names, and bin/config/rulesets.yaml with the three rulesets: master (stage development: no pull request and no required check, direct pushes allowed; stage production: pull request, the aggregate check named check, squash merge only, linear history), release (pull request, linear history, no deletion, no force push, the App as the only bypass actor) and legacy (the release rules for the branch patterns the project names). Every ruleset is plain GitHub ruleset JSON built with the library json functions; the stage comes from the setting GIT_WORKFLOW_STAGE of the project-root .env, read from the environment, default development in code, and an unknown stage is refused. The bypass actor id is the placeholder APP_ID_PLACEHOLDER, which rules-sync replaces with the value of GIT_WORKFLOW_APP_ID before it sends a ruleset. tests/git-rules/build.sh checks the JSON of every name and stage with jq.
brief.output: bin/lib/rules.sh, bin/config/rulesets.yaml and tests/git-rules/build.sh.
brief.pattern: bin/lib/tool.sh: the layout of a plugin library

tasks.title: Write the rules-sync command: apply the rulesets as the App

inputs.why: rules_json and rules_names, the rulesets this command applies
token_fetch, the token with the administration set
the classic command this one replaces
remote_slug, the owner/name of the remote of the repository the rulesets are applied to

verify.from: environment fact: the dry run changes nothing, the apply fetches the token with the administration set before its first write, a second apply changes nothing, the stage selects the master ruleset and the App id comes from GIT_WORKFLOW_APP_ID
verify.run: bash -n bin/modules/git/rules-sync.sh && bash tests/git-rules/sync.sh && for k in 'dry-run' 'second apply' 'stage' 'GIT_WORKFLOW_APP_ID' 'token' 'skipped'; do grep -qi -- "$k" tests/git-rules/sync.sh || exit 1; done

tasks.why: The rulesets reach GitHub from one command with the App as the writer, in both phases (decisions D26 and D30 of the concept).
tasks.result: The command app git rules-sync that creates or updates the rulesets of a repository.
tasks.done: The dry run prints per ruleset whether it would be created or updated and sends nothing; the apply fetches the token with the administration set before its first write and creates or updates each ruleset by name; a second apply changes nothing. The test covers the dry run without a write, the token before the first write, the second apply, the stage and the App id. A ruleset whose branch setting is unset is skipped and reported, and master still applies.
tasks.fails: The rulesets would be applied with a personal token, a repeated apply would create duplicates, or the master ruleset of the wrong stage would be applied.

brief.arguments: Write app git rules-sync [--dry-run|--apply] [--stage <stage>]: for the repository of the remote origin it builds the rulesets with rules_json, reads the existing rulesets of the repository through gh by name, and prints per ruleset create, update or unchanged. --apply fetches the token (permission set administration) before its first write and creates or updates the rulesets through the Rulesets API, never deleting a ruleset it did not name. tests/git-rules/sync.sh runs the dry run against a stub gh that returns canned ruleset lists and checks the three outcomes. The slug of the repository comes from remote_slug of the remote library (T4.18), never from a copy of the helper of release.sh. The stage comes from --stage or GIT_WORKFLOW_STAGE, default development; the bypass actor id comes from GIT_WORKFLOW_APP_ID of the project-root .env, required for --apply (refused with a message when empty) and left as the placeholder in the dry run. The stub gh of tests/git-rules/sync.sh appends every call to a log, and the test asserts: the dry run logs no write; --apply logs the token request before its first create or update; a second --apply, with the stub returning the created rulesets, logs no write (a second apply changes nothing); --stage production and --stage development send different master rulesets; the bypass actor id equals GIT_WORKFLOW_APP_ID. The throwaway repository holds an empty .agentic-os directory. A ruleset whose branch setting is unset is skipped, not applied: release without GIT_WORKFLOW_RELEASE_BRANCH and legacy without GIT_WORKFLOW_LEGACY_BRANCHES, for which rules_json exits 3 (decisions D16 and D31). rules-sync prints skipped for it and goes on, the master ruleset always applies, and the run exits 0 when only skips happened. tests/git-rules/sync.sh adds the case: a project with neither setting applies master and prints skipped for release and legacy.
brief.output: bin/modules/git/rules-sync.sh and tests/git-rules/sync.sh; the registration in module.yaml is the task T4.7. branch-protection.sh stays until the retirement phase.
brief.pattern: bin/modules/git/promote.sh: the layout of a command that fetches a token and calls the API

phases.title: Monorepo
phases.intent: Release each component on its own, split components marked split: yes with splitsh-lite, baseline the existing child repositories and apply --latest=false in multi-component repositories (roadmap milestone m5-monorepo).

phases.title: Retire the old approach
phases.intent: Remove the old CI except status-checks.yml, replace the classic protection code, and correct the stale project context wording (roadmap milestone m6-retire-old).

decisions.question: Which phases the plan details
decisions.chosen: P1 is detailed; P2 to P6 are outlined, one per later milestone of the roadmap
decisions.reason: P2 to P6 depend on the checks of P1. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Where the check reports and design notes are written
decisions.chosen: .agentic-os/project/concepts/git-workflow-plugin/notes/
decisions.reason: It lies inside the project scope trigger and next to the concept's raw input. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: How the GitHub App behaviours are checked
decisions.chosen: A test GitHub App installed on a sandbox repository that the developer registers before T1.1 starts
decisions.reason: The behaviours cannot be checked by reading documentation alone. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: How the token service authenticates a developer (CONCEPT-git-workflow-plugin D48, left to the plan)
decisions.chosen: An existing gh login checked against organisation membership
decisions.reason: The white paper's recommendation in row Q-G; it needs no new credential on a developer machine. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: What happens when the token service is down
decisions.chosen: Fail closed: no App write happens while the service is down
decisions.reason: Concept decision D30 leaves no human write path, and a manual token would reopen the personal-token problem. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Format of the component declaration (CONCEPT-git-workflow-plugin D44, left to the plan)
decisions.chosen: One structured file at the repository root with explicit lists for checks and version files, and no kind field
decisions.reason: The white paper's recommendation in row Q-O. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Whether JS components take their paths from the workspace graph (CONCEPT-git-workflow-plugin D46)
decisions.chosen: Yes: the workspace graph and turbo --affected; other components list paths in the declaration
decisions.reason: The white paper's recommendation in row Q-R. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: How pre-releases are handled (CONCEPT-git-workflow-plugin D47)
decisions.chosen: Settled after T1.2 reports white paper line 390 (the git-cliff pre-release counter); T1.4 writes the answer into its note
decisions.reason: The white paper's row Q-H says verify first, and T1.4 depends on T1.2. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: How the plan's tasks are carried out
decisions.chosen: inline
decisions.reason: No task is bash or hook code, T1.1 needs the developer's own account, and T1.3 and T1.4 are dialogue. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Whether T1.3 also settles where the token service runs and who holds the App key
decisions.chosen: Yes: the token service note gets a Service hosting section naming the hosting and the key custody
decisions.reason: The m1 gate says the token service is settled, and concept D6 says the App private key never reaches a developer machine. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Which task owns the white paper lines 411 and 654
decisions.chosen: T1.1 takes both lines; its report holds eleven rows
decisions.reason: Both are GitHub latest-release behaviour under concept decision D56; the white paper marks 18 lines and no task owned these two. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: How the verify runs prove the notes
decisions.chosen: The verify runs test content: the result column of each row, a named decision on refuted or changed rows of T1.1, the citation of L500 in the token service note and of L390 in the component declaration note, and no TBD, TODO or open question
decisions.reason: A structure-only check passed empty or TBD notes. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: How the sandbox prerequisite of plan decision D3 is enforced
decisions.chosen: A developer-owned task T1.0 writes sandbox.md; T1.1 depends on it
decisions.reason: No task or dependency encoded the order. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: What the P1 gate proves
decisions.chosen: The gate runs the verify.run of every P1 task (T1.0 to T1.4), each in its own subshell, joined with &&
decisions.reason: A test -s over the notes passed one-row notes and could not see a missing line or the sandbox note; the milestone gate m1-foundations needs the coverage and content proofs. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Where the token service runs (corrects D10, which had the note name the hosting)
decisions.chosen: The platform is not chosen now: the note fixes the requirements the platform must meet (HTTPS endpoint, private key only in the service's secret store, no logging of tokens, rejection of non-members) and the platform is chosen before the release core phase (P3) is detailed
decisions.reason: The developer chose to name the hosting later and gave no infrastructure to name. Consequence: the milestone gate m1-foundations is met for the contract, the authentication, the fallback and the key custody, not for the hosting platform.

decisions.question: Who holds the production App private key
decisions.chosen: The key exists only in the service's secret store, with no backup; an org owner generates it and rotates it by generating a new key and deleting the old one; a lost key is replaced, not recovered
decisions.reason: Fewest copies, least exposure; GitHub lets an org owner generate a new key at any time and keep several keys active. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: The contract between the CLI and the token service
decisions.chosen: The CLI sends the developer's gh login token, the repository and the permission set the command needs; the service checks the login and the organisation membership and returns an installation token narrowed to that repository and permission set, valid for the one hour GitHub fixes; the CLI keeps it in memory, hands it to the tool container as an environment variable by name, never writes it to disk and drops it after the command
decisions.reason: The one-hour lifetime and the narrowing by repository and permissions were measured on 2026-11-03; a membership check works with the developer's repo-scoped login. Developer answer, approved as stated.

decisions.question: How pre-releases are handled in detail (the answer D8 deferred to the result of T1.2)
decisions.chosen: A pre-release has a release commit like a final release, made by `release <component> --pre <channel>`; the version files carry the pre-release version; the CLI composes the first -<channel>.1 from the base version and git-cliff counts the following ones
decisions.reason: git-cliff 2.8.0 has no --pre and cannot start a pre-release line, but increments an existing one (row L390); one mechanism keeps the tag equal to package.json. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Name and syntax of the component declaration file
decisions.chosen: components.yaml at the repository root, YAML, read on the host with yq
decisions.reason: Matches the white paper's sketch in Appendix B and decision D6 (a structured file at the repository root); the tool image needs no parser. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: How modules call the tool image (the plan part of concept decision D55)
decisions.chosen: An ephemeral container per call (docker run --rm), with the mounts of the call; no long-running container
decisions.reason: Measured on 2026-11-03: about 0.5 s per ephemeral call against about 0.1 s per docker exec. Mounts of a long-running container are fixed at its start, so a worktree outside them breaks, and the plugin would have to manage that container and replace it when the image changes. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Which platforms the tool image supports
decisions.chosen: linux/amd64 only, pinned in the compose file; an arm64 host runs it through Docker's emulation, which is not measured
decisions.reason: The only splitsh-lite release (v1.0.1) has a linux amd64 binary and none for arm64 (row L595 of verify-tools.md), and the arm64 download of the Dockerfile returns 404. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Where the pinned versions, the base image digest and the checksums live
decisions.chosen: In the plugin settings bin/config/env.defaults with keys PLUGIN_EDOTZ_GIT_WORKFLOW_*, overridable by the .env file in the project root; the compose file and the library function read the same values
decisions.reason: Developer answer in free text: use the plugin config and its corresponding overwrite .env in the project root. Read as the existing file env.defaults, not as a new file with a leading dot; to be confirmed with the approval of this amendment.

decisions.question: Who carries out the tasks of P2 (supersedes D9 for this plan)
decisions.chosen: The bash tasks go to bash-author through /aos:bash-authoring with a review; the Dockerfile, the compose file and the pins are written inline; the clean machine check is the developer's. The mode header of the plan becomes subagents.
decisions.reason: The framework prescribes the authoring pipeline for bash code; the tasks of P1 were research notes, which fitted inline. Developer answer, recommended option.

decisions.question: Where the pinned versions, the base image digest and the checksums live, after D22
decisions.chosen: In .env.defaults in the plugin root, with unprefixed keys (IMAGE_BASE, GH_VERSION and so on); a consuming project does not override them, and bin/config/env.defaults keeps only the settings a project may override through its .env
decisions.reason: Developer correction on 2026-11-03: the pins are plugin internals read by the compose file and the library function, while the plugin config in bin/config is the overridable part. The framework loads only the file name env.defaults from bin/config, so that file keeps its name.

decisions.question: Where the token service runs, after D15 deferred it
decisions.chosen: As a Docker container on the developer's own machine, with the service code and its configuration (organisation, App ID, permission set of each command) in the image; the App's private key is a read-only file on the host, mounted into the container at run time and never part of an image, a repository or a log; the other requirements of the note stay (HTTPS endpoint, no token logging or storing, refusal of non-members, narrowed tokens only)
decisions.reason: Developer answer on 2026-11-03: run it on this machine as a Docker container holding all needed information and configuration; for the key the developer chose the mounted secret, not the image. This machine is the one declared exception to the note's rule that the key is not on a developer machine; D16 holds otherwise (one copy, no backup, an organisation owner rotates it). Consequence under D5: while this machine or the container is down, nobody releases, and developers on other machines reach the service only through an endpoint this machine exposes, which is still to be settled.

decisions.question: Who reaches the token service, which D25 left open
decisions.chosen: Only this machine: the service listens on the local machine and is not exposed to other machines, no tunnel and no certificate; its purpose is to learn how it works and to be able to change it
decisions.reason: Developer answer on 2026-11-03. It closes the open point of D25. Consequence: the release commands work on this machine only, and a developer on another machine cannot get a token (D5, fail closed). A shared or exposed endpoint is a later decision that supersedes this one.

decisions.question: In which language the token service is written
decisions.chosen: Node with Octokit (@octokit/auth-app): the App JWT, the installation token request and its narrowing come from the maintained library; a small HTTP server in its own image under token-service/ that holds code and configuration, the key mounted as a host file (D25); the tool image stays free of Node (concept D34)
decisions.reason: Developer chose the recommended option on 2026-11-03: the security-critical parts are not hand-rolled.

decisions.question: Whether the release notes carry an LLM summary in P3 (concept D49)
decisions.chosen: No: the release commit, the CHANGELOG and the GitHub Release body come from git-cliff alone and are deterministic; a summary through provider_run_prompt on the host (concept D18) is a later addition
decisions.reason: Developer chose the recommended option on 2026-11-03: the m3 gate does not depend on an LLM.

decisions.question: What the release does to the README
decisions.chosen: It rewrites only the lines between the markers <!-- release:start --> and <!-- release:end --> (a version badge and a release link: releases/tag/<tag> of the component, in a single repository the same link form); the rest of the README stays the author's; a README without the markers is left untouched and the release says so
decisions.reason: Developer chose the recommended option on 2026-11-03: no template and no generation, which the concept leaves out of scope (D20).

decisions.question: How the token service is laid out in the plugin, after D27
decisions.chosen: Node with Octokit as before (D27), but as a module command: bin/modules/git/token-service.mjs with the shebang #!/usr/bin/env node, registered in module.yaml as app git token-service with requires node; its dependency @octokit/auth-app in the package.json of the plugin root; its configuration in bin/config/token-service.json; its image and compose file in the .docker directory (.docker/token-service.Dockerfile, .docker/compose.token-service.yaml); its check in tests/token-service/check.sh; the key stays a mounted host file (D25)
decisions.reason: Developer feedback on 2026-11-03: the modules may run Node through the shebang, a package.json belongs in the project directory and the Docker configuration in .docker. The dispatcher is polyglot: the interpreter comes from the shebang.

decisions.question: Which linter the Node lint command runs
decisions.chosen: Biome: the command app lint node of the plugin tier (bin/modules/lint/node.sh, added to the framework's lint domain) runs Biome over the Node files in the modes staged, changed, full and specific; Biome is an exactly pinned devDependency (@biomejs/biome 2.6.4) in the package.json of the plugin root with its configuration in biome.json at the root
decisions.reason: Developer answer on 2026-11-03, recommended option: the old status-checks.yml already runs biome in the consuming projects, so one tool and one configuration. app lint all is a framework command and does not run the Node linter; it has to be called on its own.

decisions.question: How the images and compose services are laid out after D30
decisions.chosen: One central .docker/Dockerfile holds a stage per image (tool, token-service); one docker-compose.yaml in the plugin root builds both services with context . and dockerfile .docker/Dockerfile, a target per service and IMAGE_BASE as build arg on both; compose commands take --env-file .env.defaults, which replaces the default .env so that a project .env cannot change the pins (D24). The root Dockerfile, .docker/compose.yaml, .docker/compose.token-service.yaml and .docker/token-service.Dockerfile are removed; the rest of D30 (module command, root package.json, bin/config/token-service.json, tests/token-service/check.sh, key as mounted host file) stands.
decisions.reason: Developer instruction on 2026-11-04: set a central Dockerfile in .docker and integrate the root docker-compose.yaml for tools and token service.

decisions.question: Whether a .env can override the pins of .env.defaults, after D24 and D32
decisions.chosen: The pins live in .env.defaults of the plugin root as the fallback; the .env of the plugin root, when it exists, overrides a pin key by key; the .env of a consuming project and the process environment do not change them, and bin/config/env.defaults keeps the settings a project may override. Compose commands take --env-file .env.defaults followed by --env-file .env when that exists, and tool_image_ensure merges the same two files and hashes the Dockerfile with the resolved pins. The layout of D32 stands: one central .docker/Dockerfile with the stages tool and token-service, one root docker-compose.yaml.
decisions.reason: Developer correction on 2026-11-04: .env.defaults is the fallback of .env, not a fixed set; the developer chose the .env of the plugin root as the overriding file.

decisions.question: Which composer.json does version_write refuse
decisions.chosen: version_write refuses a listed composer.json only when it has no version key and aligns it when it has one, as the component declaration note says; the brief wording refused when listed is read that way
decisions.reason: The author of the version library followed the note; the developer approved on 2026-11-04

decisions.question: What version_next returns when nothing is new
decisions.chosen: version_next prints nothing and returns status 1 when no commit of the component is newer than its latest tag; a caller reads it with if v=$(version_next ...), because a plain assignment ends under the ERR trap
decisions.reason: A commit outside every component bumps none; developer approved on 2026-11-04

decisions.question: How often a command calls token_fetch
decisions.chosen: A command calls token_fetch once per run; token_drop unsets GH_TOKEN even when it was exported, and the installation token is not exported, so a second call in the same shell finds no developer login when that login was an exported GH_TOKEN; a command that needs two permission sets runs two processes
decisions.reason: The token service contract is one request per command run; developer approved on 2026-11-04

decisions.question: Does the release commit run the hooks of the repository
decisions.chosen: No: release.sh makes the release commit with core.hooksPath=/dev/null in the tool container, because the hooks of a repository run on the host (the pre-commit hook calls agentic-os) and are not in the tool image; the message is generated and conventional and the minimum check linted the commits before; a failed commit restores the files the release wrote
decisions.reason: The first pilot apply in the sandbox stopped at the release commit on the hook; developer decision on 2026-11-04

decisions.question: What app git commit does
decisions.chosen: commit stages the named paths, takes the message from --message or asks provider_run_prompt of the host session for a conventional message from the staged diff, shows it, lints it with lint-commit and commits only after the developer confirmed; the plugin calls no provider binary (concept D10 and D18)
decisions.reason: Developer answer of 2026-11-04 to the question what commit does in P4

decisions.question: Who acts in app git start and app git pr
decisions.chosen: start makes a worktree and the branch <type>/<name> from the main branch; pr runs the minimum check, pushes the branch and opens the pull request with gh as the developer, with the developer login and not the App token; the squash merge is the developer's
decisions.reason: Developer answer of 2026-11-04

decisions.question: What app git rules-sync applies
decisions.chosen: Three rulesets from one YAML: the master ruleset with the STAGE switch (development: direct pushes, no checks; production: pull request, the aggregate check named check, squash merge), the release-branch ruleset and the legacy-branch ruleset (pull request, linear history, the App as the only bypass actor), applied as the App with the administration permission set; branch-protection.sh and its classic code stay until the retirement phase
decisions.reason: Developer answer of 2026-11-04

decisions.question: Where the check list of the PR gate and the pre-push guard comes from
decisions.chosen: One definition: the checks field of components.yaml with the commit lint of the commits since the last tag. app git check runs it for the pre-push hook and for the developer; the aggregate job check of status-checks.yml reads the same components.yaml and runs the same two steps in the runner itself, because a consuming project's runner has neither agentic-os nor this plugin
decisions.reason: Developer chose components.yaml as the single definition on 2026-11-04; the runner detail is the orchestrator's reading and is for the developer to confirm; the developer confirmed the runner detail on 2026-11-09

decisions.question: Where the slash-command wrappers of the plugin enter the plan
decisions.chosen: One new task T4.13 in P4, owner dynamic-author, depending on T4.7; T4.12 depends on it and the P4 gate gains its verify
decisions.reason: Developer chose the recommended option on 2026-11-04. The id rule forbids renumbering, and a phase after P6 could not be a dependency of the pilot T4.12. T4.13 depends on T4.7 only, not on T4.10 and T4.11 as the option text said, because the wrapped set of D43 leaves workflow-status and branch-cleanup out.

decisions.question: Which commands of app git get a slash command
decisions.chosen: Seven: /git:start, /git:commit, /git:pr, /git:check, /git:release, /git:promote and /git:rules-sync; workflow-status, branch-cleanup, lint-commit, worktree and token-service stay app-only, and split joins when P5 builds it
decisions.reason: Developer chose the recommended option on 2026-11-04 over only the four named and over every command. It extends concept decision D41, which fixes the surface as app git <command> and does not mention slash commands; it does not contradict it.

decisions.question: How the targets of the plugin commands and of the pre-push hook are named in the plan
decisions.chosen: The tier resolution functions give them: bash app tiers registration-dir commands for the registration of T4.13 and bash app tiers hook-target <path> for the hook of T4.9; no brief writes a tier path as a rule
decisions.reason: Developer answer on 2026-11-04: the existing tier resolution function considers the purpose and returns the target directory of the purpose. Checked here: registration-dir ignores a path and prints .agentic-os/commands/commands.yaml under the purpose project and commands/commands.yaml under the purpose deliverable; hook-target resolves the plugin tier from a path inside the plugin root. The T4.13 verify fails when the registration lands in the project tier. Open: whether a session with the purpose deliverable can claim T4.13 of this plan was not checked.

decisions.question: How the plugin lint module (T3.9 to T3.11) relates to the toolchain linters of project.yaml
decisions.chosen: The plugin lint module is gone: linting runs through toolchain.linters of project.yaml (node with Biome, shell) and app lint all full replaces app lint node full; the done tasks T3.9 to T3.11 stay as history and the P3 gate drops its two lint-node segments
decisions.reason: The module was removed and committed on 2026-11-05; a gate that runs bin/modules/lint/node.sh could never pass again, and a revision that names a P3 task re-runs it; the developer chose the decision plus the gate fix on 2026-11-09

decisions.question: Where the main branch and the release branch settings of the plugin come from, now that workflow.env is removed
decisions.chosen: GIT_WORKFLOW_MAIN_BRANCH and GIT_WORKFLOW_RELEASE_BRANCH, defined in the .env files of the consuming project, with master as the fallback in code; both PLUGIN_EDOTZ_GIT_WORKFLOW_ keys leave bin/config/env.defaults and release, promote, workflow-status, branch-cleanup, worktree and workflow-setup read the new names; STALE_DAYS and VSCODE_PROFILES_DIR keep their PLUGIN_ keys
decisions.reason: The developer chose the GIT_WORKFLOW_ prefix on 2026-11-09 because a consuming project defines these variables in its own .env files; the framework prefix rule of docs/configuration.md governs only the keys of the plugin's bin/config/env.defaults

decisions.question: What happens to workflow-setup.sh after the removal of workflow.env
